title: You respected Him.
paragraphs: And that’s the most dangerous place to stand.

Because you can be close enough to Jesus to feel something…
and still far enough to miss everything.

You can admire His words.
Quote His teachings.
Even defend His name.
There’s a tension in that image.

A man on his knees. Dust in his mouth. Tears cutting through the dirt on his face.
One hand on his chest… the other reaching out.
But not everyone around him is.
Because that’s what we do when Jesus gets too real.
We label Him… instead of worship Him.

In Luke 7:16, the crowd saw Jesus raise the dead and said:
“A great prophet has arisen among us!”

Because calling Jesus a prophet feels respectful…
but it can still be rebellion in disguise.
Because a prophet speaks for God.
But Jesus didn’t just speak for God.

Colossians 1:15 says:
“He is the image of the invisible God…”

John 1:14 declares:
“The Word became flesh and dwelt among us…”
This is the Message wrapped in flesh.
And here’s where it cuts deep.
Some of us are like the crowd.
We’ve reduced Jesus to something safe.
Something we can listen to… without surrendering to.
Something we can quote… without obeying.
Something we can admire… without dying to ourselves.
But Jesus never gave us that option.

In Matthew 16:15, He asks the question that still echoes today:
“But who do you say that I am?”
Who do YOU say He is?

Peter answered in Matthew 16:16:
“You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Because salvation begins where opinion ends.
Here’s the truth most people avoid:
If Jesus is just a prophet…
Then your sin is still yours.
And the cross becomes nothing more than a tragic story.
But if Jesus is the Son of God…
Because the cross was not an accident.

Isaiah 53:5 says:
“He was pierced for our transgressions; He was crushed for our iniquities…”
That means your sin had a price.
But here’s the part we don’t like.
You don’t receive that grace by admiration.
By turning from sin and trusting in Christ alone.

Acts 3:19 says:
“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.”
He represents a moment many of us are avoiding.

The moment where admiration collapses…
and surrender begins.

Where you stop saying, “I respect Jesus”…
and finally say, “Jesus is Lord.”

Romans 10:9 says:
“If you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.”
Jesus is not standing far away to shame you.
He’s standing there to receive you.
Even after calling Him everything except Lord.
So let me ask you the question that refuses to stay quiet:
Or are you ready to surrender?
Because there is a difference between knowing about Jesus…
Call Him what He truly is.
If this pierced something in you, don’t ignore it.
